faq.a: Clippers have a tiny motor that moves the blades very fast. That makes the buzz.

faq.q: What can I say at the hairdresser?
faq.a: You can say, Can you use scissors, please? or Can we have a short pause? or Please tell me before you start.
asks: Tell me about Ask for a change
Tell me about Ask for a pause

faq.q: Why does my neck feel itchy?
faq.a: Tiny cut hairs land on your skin. A soft brush or a cape helps. They wash away later.
Hairdressers want you to feel comfy and look good. They are glad when you tell them what helps.
asks: Will they be cross if I ask?

faq.q: What helps me get ready for a haircut?
faq.a: Visit the shop first to look around, watch someone else, or bring ear defenders. A grown-up you trust can help.

facts: Hair does not have feeling nerves, so cutting it does not hurt.
Electric hair clippers have blades that move side to side very quickly.

quiz.say: The clippers feel too loud for Tom. What can he ask?
quiz.show: 🔊 The clippers are too loud. What can Tom ask?
quiz.why: Scissors are quieter than clippers. A polite ask helps the hairdresser help Tom.

wrong.0: Go away can upset the hairdresser, and Tom still needs help.
wrong.2: A sweet leaves the clippers just as loud.

quiz.say: Little hairs make Mei's neck itchy. What can help?
quiz.show: Mei's neck feels itchy. What can help?
quiz.why: A soft brush moves the little hairs off her skin. The itchy feeling gets less.

wrong.1: Scratching hard can make her skin sore.
wrong.2: Running out of the shop is unsafe, and the haircut is unfinished.
